newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Finmin reaffirms Portuguese pledge to join euro.
newsitem.headline: Finmin reaffirms Portuguese pledge to join euro.

text.p: Portugal's Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco reiterated his country's determination to join the euro and again ruled out a referendum on membership of the European single currency.
"The idea of a referendum (sought by the small opposition Communist Party) comes at the wrong time," Sousa Franco told a parliamentary debate on the euro.

"This policy (to join the euro from the start) was decided legitimately when parliament ratified the Maastricht Treaty," he said. "It would be a profound disrespect for the representative democracy (parliament) to hold a referendum on the single currency," he added.
Prime Minister Antonio Guterres has repeatedly said that Portugal did not plan to hold a referendum on joining the euro.
Sousa Franco said: "This option (to join the euro) will put Portugal into the centre of European affairs."
The Communist Party, which holds just 15 seats in the 230-seat parliament and opposes the euro, called today's debate.
